$comment: Every colour, font, metric, motion, curve, material and type token a Lisa surface may use. This file is the source of truth; the framework repository's tokens/tokens.json is a copy of it and the site's check reports drift.

violet-500.role: PRIMARY UI: buttons, toggles, links, the L tile

accent.$comment: User-selectable accent set. Olive is the default; violet is demoted to one choice among many. Each accent ships the same three stops the brand does: -700 for text and solid fills on light ground (AA 4.5+ with warm-white), -500 for controls and selection outlines on light ground (3.0+), -300 for text, solid fills and selection outlines on dark ground. $solid and $selectionOutline are machine-readable scheme pairings; consumers never mix stops by eye. Every value is measured, not picked by eye. Until 2026-10-06 hues were screened to stay at least 25 degrees clear of every reserved meaning (egress #E66100, warning #E0A030, error #D6453C, success #3E9B6B), which excluded mint, green, amber, orange, red, rose and brown and left the set cool-weighted; the owner retired that screening on 2026-10-06 when the set grew from thirteen to twenty-six to cover the hue wheel ($rules.accentSet). Names are prefixed because gen-tokens.py flattens every group into one LisaColors class and bare names would collide with the account palette.

accent-olive-700.role: DEFAULT accent - the house colour - text on light

accent-olive-500.role: DEFAULT accent - the house colour - controls

accent-olive-300.role: DEFAULT accent - the house colour - text on dark

accent-violet-700.role: the legacy brand violet, still selectable - text on light

accent-violet-500.role: the legacy brand violet, still selectable - controls

accent-violet-300.role: the legacy brand violet, still selectable - text on dark

accent-walnut-700.role: earth, yellowish brown - text on light

accent-walnut-300.role: earth, yellowish brown - text on dark

accent-chestnut-700.role: earth, reddish brown - text on light

accent-chestnut-300.role: earth, reddish brown - text on dark

accent-sand-700.role: earth, the warm counterpart of slate - text on light

accent-sand-500.role: earth, the warm counterpart of slate - controls

accent-sand-300.role: earth, the warm counterpart of slate - text on dark

accent-emerald-700.role: green, between moss and green - text on light

accent-emerald-500.role: green, between moss and green - controls

accent-emerald-300.role: green, between moss and green - text on dark

accent-azure-700.role: blue, between sky and blue - text on light

accent-azure-500.role: blue, between sky and blue - controls

accent-azure-300.role: blue, between sky and blue - text on dark

accent-plum-700.role: purple, between orchid and pink - text on light

accent-plum-500.role: purple, between orchid and pink - controls

accent-plum-300.role: purple, between orchid and pink - text on dark

accent-copper-700.role: earth, between orange and sand - text on light

accent-copper-500.role: earth, between orange and sand - controls

accent-copper-300.role: earth, between orange and sand - text on dark

ink-950.role: the shadow of raised paper under dark: slate-950, a step below the dark ground (ink-900 is that ground, so a shadow in it draws nothing — the owner at the seat, 2026-09-26); blue-tinted, never black

glass-rim.role: the Dock's fine rim and every dialog paper's: white at glass-rim-alpha, one pixel on the surface's own edge (the owner, 2026-10-24, i339)

paper.role: light app background — slate-100, the light ground (the dark ground is dark.base, slate-900)

surface.role: light cards — slate-50; light and dark are variations of slate, never white or black (owner, 2026-09-17)

error-soft.role: error/warning text on dark surfaces, where error-500 loses contrast (consent warnings)

window.$comment: Window furniture only. These values were measured from the owner's current macOS Retina reference on 2026-08-11; they are not semantic status colours.

egress.role: EXACTLY ONE MEANING: 'this leaves your hardware'. Remote/offload actions and their consent toggles. Never brand, never generic UI.

mode.$comment: Per-mode accent for the Assistant navrail (#180/#182). Siblings of brand violet-500 — same lightness/saturation, hue shifted — so the family reads as one, not four. WHICH MODE, not status. Applied narrowly: the rail's selected pill and the composer focus ring, nothing else. Chat is the brand anchor unchanged.

mode-chat.role: Chat — brand violet-500 unchanged, the anchor

account.$comment: Per-account identity colours (#248). IDENTITY, NOT STATUS: these say which mailbox, never whether something is wrong. Deliberately distinct from color.semantic — an account tinted error-red would read as a failure every time you looked at the rail. Assigned by hashing a stable key (the Maildir root), not by position, so adding an account never recolours the others.

violet.role: brand violet-500; the first account gets the house colour

tag.$comment: The seven tag colours, the reference platform's, as Files' Tags rows and (when tags are true) the item dots draw them; an application names them by token, never by literal (the owner's rule: fix at the framework level).

ui.role: the OS font: UI, body, headings

mono.role: Ledger, code, model ids, hashes — Lisa's monospace. Was the literal string 'monospace' until 2026-08-13, which meant Lisa had no mono identity at all: fontconfig picked, and on the reference device it picked Noto Sans Mono. Shipped as STATIC instances under /usr/share/fonts/jetbrains-mono for the same reason Rubik is (#161). NOTE: the weight roles below are calibrated to RUBIK's optical weight; JetBrains Mono has not been judged on hardware yet, so it uses its own numeric weights until it is.

metric.$comment: Geometry shared by GTK, Shell and web renderers. Values are logical pixels; renderers apply the session scale. The names are roles, not an invitation for callers to invent in-between numbers.

radius-control.role: buttons, entries and navigation rows; inner radius of a concentric card pair

radius-sheet.role: Content ground inside glass chrome. Equals radius-control today by coincidence, not by rule: a sheet is not a control, and tuning one must not move the other.

radius-frame.role: framed inputs and compact surfaces; inner radius of a concentric panel pair

radius-window.role: the window's own corner; 12 logical px is the LisaOS native window frame, shared by client clipping and compositor effects

radius-card.role: cards and boxed lists; radius-control + space-1 for a 4px concentric inset

outline-width.role: the accent outline a destination shows while a drag hovers it (a Tile outlined, a scheme selected); never a material border

radius-panel.role: launcher, raised glass and major floating panels; radius-frame + space-2 for an 8px concentric inset

radius-pill.role: badges and true pill controls only

border-hairline.role: structural and semantic separation only; not a material outline

material-edge-blur.role: zero-offset ambient shadow replacing hard borders on glass and raised surfaces

slider-thumb.role: the Slider's handle diameter at rest

slider-thumb-hover.role: the Slider's handle diameter while the pointer is over the control or a drag is on — it grows so it is easy to grab (the owner, 2026-10-01)

switch-height.role: the Switch's track height; the knob is the height less space-1

checkbox-size.role: the Checkbox's box and the Radio's circle

chrome-height.role: compact integrated app titlebar and toolbar height

window-toolbar-height.role: full-width app header containing traffic lights, the title immediately after them and toolbar controls

chrome-control.role: icon and text controls inside compact app chrome

nav-rail-width.role: navigation rail and leading window-semaphore cell width

nav-rail-compact-width.role: icon-only navigation rail inside a shared window glass surface

tab-max-width.role: the widest a tab's label run — the label with the control's horizontal padding — may be. A tab is sized to its content and capped here, and the selection and close hit targets are reserved outside the cap, so a tab carrying a close target is at most 284 wide and a title never truncates earlier for having a close button. A strip of few tabs ends after the last tab instead of dividing the band, and crowding scrolls the strip rather than shrinking a target

widget-unit.role: one widget cell. small is one unit square; medium is two units wide; large is two units square, at n*unit + (n-1)*gap. Sizes are the system's so widgets align to each other on the desktop, never each widget's own choice (ADR-0030). COUPLED TO THE DOCK: 168 is exactly 3 x dock-app-icon, so widget widths land on the dock's rhythm. That was not derived originally and is kept deliberately; change either number and check the other

widget-gap.role: space between widget cells. A multi-unit widget spans units plus the gaps between them, so 2 units wide is 358 rather than 336

settings-narrow-breakpoint.role: Settings compact mode reduces content density below this width; navigation remains a dismissible overlay until the two-pane breakpoint

settings-two-pane-breakpoint.role: Settings adaptive mode switches from a dismissible navigation overlay to persistent navigation and detail panes

settings-row-min-height.role: two-line Settings device and status row floor

settings-wallpaper-preview-height.role: Appearance wallpaper choice preview height at the built-in 16:10 aspect ratio

avatar-row.role: account identity image in a list row

avatar-greeter.role: primary account identity image in authentication UI

icon-compact.role: compact inline state and menu icon

icon-identity.role: application, device and account identity icon

window-control.role: close, minimize and zoom traffic-light diameter: macOS measures 14, Lisa's are a bit bigger on the owner's word (2026-10-08: traffic lights a bit bigger, icons bigger)

window-control-gap.role: visible gap between traffic lights; with the diameter the centre step stays 23, so the title's place does not move

drag-threshold.role: movement past which a press becomes a drag; a shaky click is still a click

dock-app-icon.role: resting application icon size in the desktop Dock

dock-app-icon-magnified.role: peak hovered application icon size, twice dock-app-icon: the Dock's default magnified size, rising out of the glass past its space4 inset without changing the Dock's outer geometry (S-281-2, 2026-09-28; 72 before)

dock-running-indicator.role: running application state dot below a Dock icon

dock-window-preview-width.role: minimized-window tile width in the desktop Dock

dock-window-preview-height.role: minimized-window tile height in the desktop Dock

glass-blur.role: full-capability glass blur; broad enough to remove readable scene detail while preserving ambient colour

shadow-popup-y.role: menu and popup shadow offset — a Select's list, a MenuPanel; short, so the panel sits just above what it opened over (the owner at the seat, 2026-10-08: "too much drop shadow")

shadow-popup-blur.role: menu and popup shadow softness: small and soft, drawn in ink-950 at shadow-alpha-light or shadow-alpha-dark by the ground — one shadow for every menu and popup

shadow-window-y.role: resting window shadow offset; an unfocused window sits closer to the desktop

shadow-window-active-y.role: focused window shadow offset; focus lifts the window off the desktop

shadow-window-active-blur.role: focused window shadow softness. Depth is how focus reads before colour does, so the two states must be obviously different rather than subtly

menu-bar.role: slim desktop menu bar height in logical pixels, independent of application toolbar height

window-resize-edge.role: native Frame resize strip thickness; shared host/compositor hit geometry, in logical pixels

window-resize-corner-reach.role: native Frame corner reach along each adjoining edge; the union of two edge strips, not an interior square

tag-dot.role: the sidebar's tag dot, a filled circle

toolbar-control.role: a toolbar control's square — the view switch's segments, the toolbar's buttons — inside the 52 px band

column-preview-image.role: the preview column's thumbnail box in Files' column view, square

menu-row-height.role: compact menu row floor; larger text or a disabled reason may grow it

motion.$comment: Durations in milliseconds. Reduced-motion renderers replace animation durations with zero and keep the state change; tooltip-delay is an interaction delay and remains intact.

hover.role: leaving a hover, and a row selection. A hover arrives at once — 0 ms, the highlight is there on the first frame the pointer is over the row — and leaves over this duration; a fade-in on hover reads as lag (the owner at the seat, 2026-09-17 18:2x)

dock-magnify.role: pointer-proximity magnification without changing Dock geometry

dock-hover-follow.role: the Dock sliding in and out when it hides; never the magnification's position, which is the pointer's within a frame (S-281-1, 2026-09-28); dock-magnify is the wave's rise and fall

window-minimize.role: a window's minimize to its Dock tile and its restore from there, which the compositor draws; a reversal mid-way takes the share of it that is left, never less than a twentieth

window-minimize-slow.role: the same minimize and restore while Shift is held, slowed for a person to watch; reduced motion makes it a cut like the other

tooltip-delay.role: intent delay before a pointer-hover label appears

toast-timeout.role: how long a toast stays before it leaves on its own; an interaction delay, kept under reduced motion

banner-timeout.role: how long a notification banner stays before it leaves on its own; an interaction delay, kept under reduced motion

feedback-timeout.role: how long the feedback overlay stays after the last volume or brightness key; an interaction delay, kept under reduced motion

dock-label-delay.role: none: the Dock's name label is there the instant the pointer is over a tile (the owner, 2026-10-05: "no delay on tooltip in dock"); kept so a caller that names it waits nothing

busy-turn.role: one full linear turn of a shared busy glyph, repeating only while its caller has a live work scope; stops on false or disposal; reduced motion keeps a static busy tint (F21:09, 2026-11-04). Resolved through Motion.named('busy-turn'), never an application timer.

curve.$comment: Cubic Bezier control points. Standard motion responds immediately and settles softly; emphasized motion gives major spatial changes a clearer arrival without bounce or overshoot. Reduced-motion renderers keep state changes but set animation durations to zero.

standard.role: hover, focus, checked state and small continuity transitions

emphasized.role: pane, dialog and whole-surface spatial transitions

linear.role: constant angular progress of busy-turn only; interactive entrance, exit and response keep standard or emphasized.

material.$comment: Unitless opacity values. These are capability-aware: high contrast uses solid surfaces and reduced transparency raises the fills.

glass-rim-alpha.role: the alpha of glass-rim: 0x30 of 255, the Dock's rim since 2026-09-12, now every dialog paper's (i339)

glass-veil.role: an application window's paper ground before its glass is proven, on a loss and on a host without glass: the scheme's ground colour; over proven glass the Frame paints no ground and the compositor's text veil (glass-tint-alpha-text) is the one veil. The value is not read as a translucent veil any more (docs /frameworks/frame/glass)

glass-accent-tint-alpha.role: the share of the person's accent (`appearance.accent`, its controls stop, `accent-<name>-500`) in the compositor's veil colour: every glass region's veil is glass-tint-light or glass-tint-dark × 0.9 + the accent × 0.1, blended in encoded sRGB — the default for every window and every piece of the Shell's chrome, not an opt-in (the owner, 2026-10-02: "glass has a small reddish [cast], same for paper, like slate + 10% red"). The tint colours the veil only; the veil's alpha is still the role's line (docs /frameworks/frame/glass#colour)

paper-accent-tint-alpha.role: the share of the person's accent (`accent-<name>-500`) in every paper ground: the scheme's slate — paper and surface under light, base and elevated under dark, and the Material surface roles a window's ground theme derives from them — × 0.9 + the accent × 0.1, blended in encoded sRGB; the inks stay slate. Reduced transparency and high contrast keep the tinted paper (docs /ui/tokens, accentTint)

widget-scrim-alpha.role: the contrast floor between a widget's own frost and its content. A widget cannot choose its wallpaper, so legibility cannot be left to it. THIS COMPOSITES OVER THE WIDGET'S OWN GLASS, NEVER ON TOP OF THE SHELL'S: stacked on a 0.85 veil the effective coverage is 91.8 percent and the wallpaper is gone, which no scrim value rescues since the veil alone hides 85. Measure the product on a real surface, not the number in this file (ADR-0030)

applet-stale-alpha.role: the opacity the compositor draws a stale applet's surface at (docs /system/desktop, lifecycle 7: stale is shown as stale, never the last frame as current). Below inactive-opacity on purpose: an applet's whole content is what went stale, and the caption beside it says since when

foreground-secondary-alpha.role: secondary labels over semantic Lisa materials

foreground-tertiary-alpha.role: captions and quiet metadata over semantic Lisa materials

interactive-hover-alpha.role: luminous hover feedback for borderless controls

interactive-selected-alpha.role: selected navigation and toggle material: the surface's own ink behind a chosen tab, a switcher or overview tile, a pressable's selected wash. Never an item's selection (selection-alpha) nor selected text (text-selection-alpha)

selection-alpha.role: a selected item's fill: the accent's controls stop (accent-<name>-500) at this alpha behind a selected row, sidebar item, rail destination, table row or column-view row, over the ground it sits on; the item's inks stay the ground's (docs /ui/22-colour, Selection; the owner 2026-11-05)

text-selection-alpha.role: selected text's highlight: the accent's controls stop at this alpha behind the selected run in every field and search field (docs /ui/22-colour, Selection; the owner 2026-11-05)

row-stripe-alpha.role: the alternate row's fill in a striped DataTable: the ground's own primary ink at this alpha, beneath the row's selection, hover and press

edge-alpha-dark.role: light edge on a dark glass surface

edge-alpha-light.role: dark edge on a light glass surface

carved-highlight-alpha.role: light half of a two-tone structural groove

carved-shadow-alpha.role: dark half of a two-tone structural groove

dialog-scrim-alpha-light.role: the scrim over a window's content while an alert or a sheet stands, under light — ink-950 at this alpha (Material 3's scrim; the owner's ruling, /ui/18-dialogs, 2026-09-26)

dialog-scrim-alpha-dark.role: the same scrim under dark — more than light, so the raised paper separates from the slate-900 ground

shadow-window-alpha.role: resting compositor window shadow; one layer on every normal app window

shadow-window-active-alpha.role: additional compositor lift layer supplied automatically to the active window

inactive-opacity.role: inactive peripheral chrome; content text is never dimmed to this

glass-tint-light.role: the compositor's veil over a window's wallpaper frost under appearance.colorScheme light — a white the chrome's light ink reads on over any wallpaper (docs /frameworks/frame/glass, 'the tint follows the appearance')

glass-tint-dark.role: the same veil under appearance.colorScheme dark; the achromatic near-black the compositor has always drawn for shell chrome

glass-tint-alpha.role: the compositor's veil over iconic glass — the Dock's tray, which carries only pictures — at appearance.glassTransparency's default 15; the iconic line runs 1.6 times it at 0 to none at 40, with no floor (docs /frameworks/frame/glass)

glass-tint-alpha-text.role: the compositor's veil over text glass — every application window's, and the Shell's chrome that carries glyphs (bar, menus, notices, consent, the feedback pill) — at appearance.glassTransparency's default 15, on two straight segments: from glass-tint-alpha-max 0.9 at 0 to this 0.83 at 15, and from it to glass-veil-floor 0.756 at 40 (a single line through 0.9 and 0.756 would give 0.846 at 15) (docs /frameworks/frame/glass)

glass-tint-alpha-max.role: the text veil at appearance.glassTransparency 0, the Less end: the densest the slider draws; glass stays glass, and solid is paper (a surface declaring none)

glass-veil-floor.role: the text veil at appearance.glassTransparency 40, the More end. Continuous encoded-sRGB contrast binds at alpha 0.753833 for light red with opaque ink-700 over black, but shader precision and RGBA8 quantization make 0.754 and 0.755 fail in the native Mesa llvmpipe readback. The selected 0.756 floor passes that actual shader path at 4.538288:1; every accent and integer stop, both schemes, are checked in native framebuffer and actual UI fallback tests. This is a tested rendering floor, not a universal GPU minimum; installed hardware proof remains owed. The earlier thirteen-accent floor was 0.75.

quick-look-fraction.role: Quick Look's share of the screen, both axes — seven tenths (the owner, 2026-09-22 02:2x); inside a window the window is the screen. No fixed width, height or image box: the picture's box is what is left under the band, and a provider is asked at that box

shadow-popup-alpha-light.role: soft external menu and popup shadow on light ground

shadow-popup-alpha-dark.role: soft external menu and popup shadow on dark ground; independent of window shadows

type.$comment: Rubik reads visually one step heavier than its numeric name in Lisa surfaces. Roles deliberately map down one cut: Light is our regular reading weight, Regular is our ordinary emphasis, and Medium is reserved for display titles.

heading-weight.role: headings, window titles and emphasized controls

body-weight.role: body copy: Rubik Light is Lisa's visual regular

$rules.noWhiteAnywhere: Light and dark are variations of slate (the owner, 2026-09-17): the light ground is `paper` (`#F1F5F9`, slate-100) and its cards `surface` (`#F8FAFC`, slate-50); the dark ground is `base` (`#0F172A`, slate-900) and its cards `elevated` (`#1E293B`, slate-800). No white, no black and no pure neutral anywhere — slate is blue-tinted, and a grey whose channels are equal is a Material default that has slipped in.
$rules.aThemeWithoutASchemeTakesThePalette: An application that passes a theme without choosing a colour scheme keeps its typography and takes Lisa's palette. A bare `ThemeData(fontFamily: …)` is how an application says *this font*, not *this palette* — but `ThemeData` always materialises a scheme, so what it silently says is Material's seeded default: `#FEF7FF` in light, a violet-tinted near-white, and `#121212` in dark, a pure neutral that gives a ground and a card the same value. On 2026-09-19 five shipped applications — Settings, Files, About, Terminal and Install — were each passing exactly that, so none of them had ever drawn Lisa's ground.
$rules.pinTheColourNotTheRelationship: A test that asserts a surface *follows the ambient scheme* stays green while the scheme is wrong, which is how this drifted for two releases after being proven on the device. Pin the colour.
$rules.accentTint: Every surface carries the person's accent at 10 % (the owner, 2026-10-02: "give a tint to every surface but very little like 10%"; "glass has a small reddish [cast], same for paper, like slate + 10% red"). Glass and paper are the scheme's slate blended with a tenth of the accent's controls stop (`accent-<name>-500`), in encoded sRGB: the compositor's veil colour is glass-tint-light or glass-tint-dark × 0.9 + accent × `glass-accent-tint-alpha`, and the dialect's paper is paper, surface, base or elevated × 0.9 + accent × `paper-accent-tint-alpha`. It is a blend over the neutral scale's own values, never an overlay that varies with what is behind. The inks stay slate, and the tint is checked against them: the text veil's floor (`glass-veil-floor`) is derived over the tinted veil with the worst accent. The tint follows an accent change in the next frame, as blur does; reduced transparency and high contrast keep paper, with the tint.
$rules.accentSet: The accent set covers the hue wheel (thirty accents since 2026-10-24, when the owner asked for the second row of the Appearance pane to be finished — emerald, azure, plum and copper joined, i353): no 30° arc of it is without an accent whose controls stop (`accent-<name>-500`) lies within 15°, measured as that stop's HSL hue (the owner's ruling, 2026-10-06: "lock them in docs" and "apply them in theme"; the set grew from thirteen accents to twenty-six, adding the warm family it lacked — a warm orange, a yellowish walnut, a chestnut — and the rest of the wheel, jade and orchid closing its last two gaps). Every accent is cut to one ramp policy, the one the first thirteen were cut to: the 500 is the controls stop; the 700 sits about 0.17 below it in HSL lightness and the 300 about 0.21 above it, each at 0.95 of its saturation, and the 500 is dark enough to keep 3.0:1 on white and on `surface` (amber, yellow and mint were darkened to it, the owner's ruling of 2026-10-06); the values are encoded sRGB, and in every ramp the 700 is darker than the 500 and the 500 darker than the 300. A picker shows the set in six families, in this order and in this order within each: warm (red, rose, terracotta, orange, amber, yellow), green (lime, olive, moss, green, jade, mint), blue (teal, cyan, sky, blue, indigo), purple (violet, purple, fuchsia, orchid, pink), earth (walnut, chestnut, sand) and neutral (slate); every accent is in exactly one family. Olive stays the default, the house accent. A retired name is never removed from the registry's enum (`appearance.accent`, [settings keys](/system/settings-keys)); a rename maps the old name to the new on this page, so a person's stored accent never breaks, and a name the registry does not know is read as olive. The tint is unchanged: every surface carries the accent's controls stop at 10 % ([accentTint](#accent-tint)).
$rules.selectionIsClear: A selection is seen at a glance, in both schemes and under every accent, as on the reference platform (the owner, 2026-11-05: selections were too faint at the accent's 22 %, i469). Two tokens draw it, both the accent's controls stop (`accent-<name>-500`) over the ground: a selected item — a row, a sidebar item, a rail destination, a table row, a column-view row — at `selection-alpha` (0.36), and selected text — in an Input, a Search field — at `text-selection-alpha` (0.40). Each value is measured, not picked by eye, over the accent-tinted grounds (paper and surface under light, base and elevated under dark) with each of the thirty accents. `selection-alpha` is the highest that keeps, for every accent on every ground: the primary ink at 7:1 or more on the fill (7.45 at the worst, lime under dark), the secondary ink at 4.5:1 under light (4.66, red) and 3:1 under dark (3.04, lime), and the keyboard focus ring at 3:1 against the selected row ([/system/accessibility](/system/accessibility), 3.21 at the worst, violet under dark); at 0.37 the dark secondary falls under 3:1. Against its ground the fill reads 1.40:1 at the worst (yellow, light) and 1.25:1 (chestnut, dark), where 0.22 gave 1.22 and 1.14. Selected text carries no secondary ink and no ring inside it, so `text-selection-alpha` sits higher, at the reference's highlight strength: the primary ink holds 7.54:1 under light and 7.04:1 under dark at the worst. A selected item wears one fill: the accent's, never the pressable's selected wash beneath it as well (a table row drew both, ink at 0.22 under the accent, and its focus ring fell to 2.09:1 under dark). `interactive-selected-alpha` stays the material of a chosen tab, a switcher or overview tile and a pressable's wash, in the surface's own ink: it marks where you are, not what you picked. The reference draws a focused list's selection as a solid accent with its text turned light; Lisa keeps the ground's inks on a translucent fill, so one row recipe holds in every scheme and no row's content must change colour with its state.

$notYetTrue: **The thirty-accent set is in `2026.11.07.1` and not yet proved at the seat** (2026-10-06, AC/AC2; `i353`, 2026-10-24; narrowed 2026-11-07, it said *not proved on a released image*): `2026.11.07.1` (`desktop/desktop` `6b3487a6`, `compositor/src/accents.rs:1-150`; `frameworks/ui` `4ebda7e9`; `apps/system/settings` `a62cb4fb`) carries the thirty-accent registry, both catalogue readers, the compositor palette and the 0.756 text veil floor. Owed at the seat: a stored new accent, the grouped selector and glass at transparency 40 in both schemes.
